Given the graph of $y=f(x)$ above, find the value of 
${\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $3$ parts: the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in [-4,-2),$ the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in (-2,0],$ and the line segment for $x\in (0,4].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-2}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={{{\int }_{-4}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-4,-2).$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle with the radius of $2$, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-2,0].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle with the radius of $2$, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot \pi \cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,4].$  The corresponding region is the trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (2+4)\cdot 4 \\  & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{3}=-12.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =\pi +\pi -12=2\pi -12.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of two line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
We divide the interval of integration into $3$ regions: the line segment for $x\in [-2,0],$ the line segment for $x\in [0,2),$ and the line segment for $x\in [2,3].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,0].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2).$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2\cdot 2) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,3].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =bh \\  & =1\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3} \\  & =2-2+2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of $y=f(x),$ shown above, consists of four line segments. Find the value of ${\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x.$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-5,-3],$ the line segment for $x\in (-3,-1),$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,1),$ and the line segments for $x\in [1,4].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-5}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{4}}
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-5,-3].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+2)2 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,-1).$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 4 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-4.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1).$ The corresponding region is a square, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & ={s}^{2} \\  & ={2}^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,4].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot 2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{4}=-3.
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}-{A}_{4} \\  & =6-4+4-3 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of four parts: the line segment for $x\in [-6,-3],$ the line segment for $x\in (-3,0],$ the line segment for $x\in (0,2],$ and the line segment for $x\in (2,5].$ Therefore, we can write the required integral as follows:

$$
{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-6}^{-3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-3}^{0}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-6,-3].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(3) \\  & =4.5.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (-3,0].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =3\cdot 1 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (0,2].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(4+2)(2) \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (2,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}(bh) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}3(6) \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-6}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =4.5+3+6+9 \\  & =22.5.\end{aligned}
$$

If the graph of $y=f(x)$ is shown above, then

${\int }_{-3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=$
{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
The graph consists of $4$ parts: the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in [-3,-1],$ the line segment for $x\in [-1,1],$ the line segment for $x\in (1,4],$ and the arc of the quarter-circle for $x\in [4,7].$ So, we can use the additive property of integrals to get

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{3}}+{{{\int }_{4}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{4}}.
$$

- The $1$st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,-1].$ The corresponding region is a combination of a rectangle and a quarter-circle of radius $2,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =bh-\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =(2)(3)-\frac{1}{4}\pi (2)^{2} \\  & =6-\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=\pi -6.
$$

- The $2$nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a rectangle, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =bh \\  & =2\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-2.
$$

- The $3$rd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in (1,4].$ The corresponding region is a trapezoid, so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{3} & =\frac{1}{2}(a+b)h \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(1+3)\cdot 3 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

- The $4$th integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [4,7].$ The corresponding region is a quarter-circle of radius $3,$ so we find the area using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{4} & =\frac{1}{4}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\pi (3)^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}-{A}_{2}+{A}_{3}+{A}_{4} \\  & =\pi -6-2+6+\frac{9\pi }{4} \\  & =-2+\frac{13\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{13\pi -8}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
